items.page_evidence: fast-address-interchange line 5-7: updates D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D take (H,D) to (H,D-H), (D,D-H), (D,H). The third update sets the D slot to (H slot) minus (D slot) = D-(D-H).
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1535-1540: the same three updates, done componentwise over Z/q^bZ with q an odd prime (lines 1398-1402, 1494-1495), send (H,D) to (D,H). Lines 1436-1442 use the same kind of identity over Z/q^bZ.
items.reason: D-(D-H)=H holds in any abelian group. It does not need 2H=0. The note's claim that this only works in characteristic 2 is false, and the paper itself uses these updates over Z/q^bZ with q odd. The quoted identities are correct.

items.page_evidence: recursive-power-saving line 15: the ratio (s/W)/m^lambda is below 1 when log_m(s/W)<lambda. Line 19: m=2, s/W=3/2, log_2(3/2)~0.585, lambda=0.8, ratio (3/2)/2^0.8~0.86.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 2416-2419: the internal sum is C e^lambda sum (a/m^lambda)^j with a=s/W<m^lambda, so the ratio a/m^lambda is below 1. Lines 170-175: s/W<m is the source of the saving.
items.reason: 2^0.8 is about 1.741, so (3/2)/2^0.8 is about 0.862. That matches the page's 0.86. The note's 1.16 is 2^0.8/(3/2), the reciprocal. The ratio is below 1, as it should be with 0.585<0.8, so the example is correct and consistent.

items.page_evidence: linear-network-roles line 5 defines rho as the permutation of roles that the scalar network applies, with each input at role w leaving at rho(w) with sign epsilon_w. Line 11 shows that frames pass through pointwise gates, and line 13 gives the telescoping.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 812-820: the implemented operator is D_out S D_in^{-1}, and when the scalar network is a signed role permutation, 'that route applies epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}'. Lines 141-147 use the same 'route ... together with its prescribed scalar sign' wording. Lines 1458-1462 and 1129 fix rho as the scalar permutation.
items.reason: The page does state that the scalar network is a signed permutation of roles (line 5), so the note's main premise misreads the page. The quoted sentence uses 'route' in the same sense as the paper (lines 141-147, 818). The paper derives this from the whole-network identity. The page leaves that identity out, but that is a gap in justification, not a misstatement.

items.page_evidence: fast-address-interchange lines 11-15: Q_k bounds the time per unit volume for fields of m^k bits. The page gives the recurrence Q_k <= (s/W)Q_{k-1}+C with s calls on volume V/W and concludes Q_k=O(u^tau) for u=m^k. The width-power hypothesis is stated. No row-count condition appears on this page. The linked roles page pads rows to a multiple of W at one level.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1475-1487: Proposition (power-width interchange) assumes e=m^k and a row field before both chunks of length divisible by W^k. Lines 1497-1503 need this for the row split. Lines 1627-1629 say it was proved 'for power widths with enough rows'. Lines 1631-1646 (Lemma chunk-swap) then give O(Vu^tau) for arbitrary bit arrays [P]x[2^u]x[G]x[2^u]x[B], with no row condition. Lines 1676-1712 do this by using high digits as rows.
items.reason: The width-power part of the note does not apply, because the page states u=m^k. The row condition is omitted, and the recurrence as written needs it at every level. But the quoted conclusion, an O(Vu^tau) interchange for fields of m^k bits, is true for every array and is established by the paper (Lemma chunk-swap, lines 1631-1646). So the statement is neither false nor wider than what the paper proves. What is missing is a justification detail of the recurrence. It is borderline because the derivation shown only works with enough rows.

items.page_evidence: subset-intersection-construction line 7: an index is iota=(T_1,T_2,T_3) in T^3, an ordered triple. Line 11: N=binom(h,3)^3. Line 16: L/N=3h^2/binom(h,3)=100/539.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 655-661: v=binom(h,3)=161700, N=v^3=4227952113000000, and the banks are indexed by a=(a_1,a_2,a_3) in T^3. Lines 1077-1081: L_b/N=100/539.
items.reason: The paper indexes by ordered triples a in T^3 and sets N=v^3=binom(h,3)^3, exactly as the page does. The note's claim that the paper treats the index as an unordered set is false. The page's ratio L/N=100/539 matches the paper, which confirms the count.

items.page_evidence: address-shear-factorization line 3 introduces H and D as two vectors of address fields and says nothing about their tape order. Line 13 does each pivot update with the additions D_tau<-D_tau+H_sigma and D_tau<-H_sigma-D_tau, then concludes 'rank_Q M interchanges plus O(V) further work'. Line 15 speaks of 'earlier' coordinates but never fixes a physical layout.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1398-1410: Lemma (cost of a rational matrix shear) assumes 'every H_i before every D_j'. Lines 1356-1358 and 551-569: linear-time updates need the target field to follow its control fields ('linear because their target field follows their control fields'). Lines 1440-1441: 'The first and last updates target a later field controlled by an earlier field.' Lines 1537-1539: the update of the earlier group, H<-H+D, is the costly one.
items.reason: The O(V) cost of the two additions comes from Lemma ordered-affine-streams, which needs the target D field to come after the control H field. In the opposite order, that update is exactly the expensive kind of operation. The page states the cost bound with no layout hypothesis, so as stated it is wider than what the paper establishes (rule c). The note is correct.

items.page_evidence: address-shear-factorization line 5: q must not divide the denominator xi, and an entry acts as mu xi^{-1} mod q^b. 'So q divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.' Line 3 only says q is a fixed odd prime.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1413-1420: the paper chooses an odd prime avoiding every denominator in the table and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor. It adds that a prime exceeding all nonzero numerators and denominators 'suffices', as an example. The triangular factors then remain invertible mod q^b.
items.reason: The requirement that q not divide denominators does not imply anything about numerators, so the 'So' is a non sequitur (rule b). The claim is also stronger than the paper's condition, which is denominators plus diagonal numerators; avoiding all numerators is only the paper's example choice. Read literally it even fails for zero entries, whose numerator 0 every q divides; the paper says 'nonzero'. The note's added complaint that the page never says which matrices or why q exists is only a justification gap, but its main point holds.

items.page_evidence: linear-network-roles line 9: the edge alpha->beta changes the stored array by D_beta D_alpha^{-1}. Line 13: the product (D_{alpha_k}D_{alpha_{k-1}}^{-1})...(D_{alpha_1}D_{alpha_0}^{-1}) = D_{alpha_k}D_{alpha_0}^{-1}.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 134-135 and 801-803: an edge from u to v applies D_v D_u^{-1}. Lines 141-144: the intermediate frames cancel and a route applies D_sink D_source^{-1}.
items.reason: With the usual right-to-left composition of operators, the rightmost factor D_{alpha_1}D_{alpha_0}^{-1} acts first, so the page's order is the order in which the edges act. Adjacent factors meet as D_{alpha_j}^{-1}D_{alpha_j}=I and cancel without any commutativity. The note reverses the composition convention.

items.page_evidence: tape-interchange line 9: F_d is the time per unit volume of a width-mu^d interchange, with s smaller calls on streams of volume V/W, so F_d <= lambda F_{d-1}+O(1). Line 11 concludes F_d=O(mu^{d tau}), which is O(u^tau) for u=mu^d. Line 3 states the general O(Vu^tau) cost. No row-count condition is given.
items.paper_evidence: Lines 1475-1487 and 1497-1503: the power-width proposition needs a row field of length divisible by W^k for the cyclic split at every level. Lines 1555-1564: the recurrence F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). Lines 1631-1646, 1676-1712 (Lemma chunk-swap): O(Vu^tau) holds for arbitrary arrays and widths after high digits are used as padded rows. Lines 1323-1345: tau=1-2^{-50}.
items.reason: The recursion as written splits into W streams at each level, which in the paper needs the W^d row condition, and the page omits it. But the quoted conclusion, an O(u^tau) cost per unit volume for width u=mu^d, holds for every array by the paper's Lemma chunk-swap. So the statement is not false and not wider than what the paper establishes. Only its derivation is incomplete. It is borderline because the recurrence presented supports the claim only when there are enough rows.

items.page_evidence: subset-intersection-construction line 7: labels are nondegenerate subspaces of F=(Q^h)^{tensor 3}, neighbors are orthogonal, and 'a label containing t_T may grow to t_S^perp, since t_T perp t_S, adding h-2 dimensions.'
items.paper_evidence: Lines 925-933: on a side wire, with the one-dimensional factor Q suppressed, the remaining component passes through P tensor <t_X> inside P tensor t_Y^perp, which is possible because t_X perp t_Y. P is a line (lines 896-898). Lines 1035-1052: edge 2->5 has residual P tensor <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2. Lines 974-976: all labels are tensored by Q.
items.reason: Read literally, a subspace of F cannot contain t_T, which lies in Q^h. But the sentence is a shorthand for the exposed tensor factor, which is exactly the paper's inclusion <t_X> in t_Y^perp. Because P and Q are lines, the full label really does gain h-2 dimensions (lines 1035-1052). The mathematics is right. The note's second complaint, that gate labels are not assigned, is only an omission of explanation. Borderline because the shorthand does not match the page's definition of a label.
